text: Matrix product and power; recurrences; transformations.

one step of the recurrence = one matrix product

A vector is a list of numbers; an n × n matrix maps vectors to vectors. The product C = A·B has C[i][j] = Σk A[i] [k]·B[k][j], O(n³). It is associative, (AB)C = A(BC), but not commutative, so Aⁿ can be computed by repeated squaring like a number (第3章): O(n³ log N).

Matrix acceleration (矩阵加速): if the next state vector is a fixed linear function of the current one, write that function as a matrix M; then stateN = MN·state0. A recurrence with N = 10¹⁸ steps becomes about 60 squarings.
Fibonacci (P1962): (Fn+1, Fn) = M·(Fn, Fn−1) with M = [[1, 1], [1, 0]]. Starting from (F1, F0) = (1, 0), Mn−1 gives Fn in its top-left entry.
The identity matrix plays the role of 1 in fast power. Write mul once with loops over k; the same code works for any size after changing 2 to the dimension.
ax = ax−1 + ax−3 (P1939): the state must hold the last three values. Row 1 of M builds the new value; the other rows just shift the old ones down.

Recipe: (1) choose a state vector holding everything the next step needs; (2) write each new entry as a combination of old ones, one row per entry; (3) power. Counting walks of length N in a graph (P2151) is the adjacency matrix to the N-th power.

Points as vectors (x, y, 1): the extra 1 lets a 3 × 3 matrix also translate. Rotation by 90° maps (x, y) to (−y, x); scaling multiplies both by k. A whole sequence of operations collapses into one matrix, applied to every point in O(1).

Order matters: a later operation T is multiplied on the left, total = T·total. Rotating then moving (1, 0) gives (0, 1) then (1, 2); moving first would give a different point. Many queries over ranges of operations combine these matrices in a segment tree.
Solving systems; no / infinite solutions; determinants mod p.

Gaussian elimination (高斯消元) solves n linear equations in n unknowns in O(n³). For each column c: pick a row with a non-zero entry in column c (the pivot, take the largest absolute value for accuracy), swap it up, divide it by the pivot, and subtract multiples of it from every other row so column c becomes 0 elsewhere.

At the end each variable sits alone in its row (Gauss-Jordan form) and the last column holds the answer. A column with no usable pivot means the system has either no solution (some row reads 0 = non-zero) or infinitely many.
31 return 0;

Check "no solution" before "infinitely many": a contradictory row wins even when there is also a free variable (P2455 is strict about this). Compare with EPS, never with == 0, because floating-point subtraction leaves tiny remainders.
Without the largest-pivot choice, dividing by a tiny pivot magnifies rounding errors and can give garbage. With a pivot of exactly 0 it divides by zero.

The determinant (行列式 , P7112) is the product of the diagonal after elimination to a triangle, with a sign flip per row swap. Modulo a non-prime p you cannot divide, so eliminate two rows against each other like Euclid's algorithm: subtract ⌊x / y⌋ times, swap, repeat. Total O(n²(n + log p)).
[[1, 2], [3, 4]] has determinant 1·4 − 2·3 = −2 ≡ 998244351. Over GF(2) (P2447 外星千足虫 , lights-out puzzles) elimination uses XOR on rows stored as bitset : 64 times faster.

Systems you have to build first: points on a sphere (P4035) give linear equations after subtracting pairs of "distance to the centre is r" equations; expected values on a graph with cycles (P2973) are n equations E = Σ p·E′ solved by elimination.
